President Bola Tinubu on Sunday donated N250m to families of victims of Friday’s boat mishap in Bayelsa State. He ordered stricter enforcement of safety standards on inland waterways as the death toll from the accident rose to 29, with more than 50 survivors. Vice President Kashim Shettima conveyed the President’s position and the donation on Sunday during a condolence visit to Government House, Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital. This is according to a statement signed on Sunday by the Senior Special Assistant to the Vice President on Media and Communications, Stanley Nkwocha, titled ‘Bayelsa Boat Mishap: President Tinubu Orders Stiffer Waterway Safety Measures.’ The accident occurred on Friday at the Oweikorogha/Otuan River Junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area, when a boat carrying scores of mourners travelling to a funeral capsized. Governor Douye Diri, who briefed the Vice President at Government House, attributed the tragedy to an alleged failure by boat operators to observe established safety protocols, describing it as avoidable. He said the state government had constituted a committee to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident. Shettima said Tinubu had also demanded a thorough investigation into the circumstances of the mishap, including preliminary reports of a possible mechanical fault. He stated, “We have received preliminary reports concerning the circumstances of this accident, including indications of a possible mechanical failure. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. We must establish what happened, identify any failures in safety procedures and take the necessary steps to prevent a recurrence.” The Vice President described the disaster as an equity issue, arguing that Nigerians who travel by water were entitled to the same standard of protection as those who travel by road or air. “We cannot accept a situation in which citizens must gamble with their lives simply to move between communities. Geography may determine how people travel, but it must never determine how much protection their lives deserve. The Vice President described the tragedy as carrying “a particular cruelty”, noting that the victims had set out to mourn the dead before death claimed them along the way. Shettima stated, “Each person lost in those waters had a name, a history, relationships and responsibilities. Somewhere, a family is struggling to understand how someone who left home for a funeral will never walk through that door again.” He assured the bereaved families that they would receive lasting support from the Federal Government. “To the families who have lost their loved ones, I will not pretend that time alone will make this pain disappear. “Our responsibility is to stand with you beyond this visit, beyond these condolences and beyond the days when this tragedy dominates the news,” he said. Before proceeding to Government House, the Vice President visited survivors receiving treatment at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital, where he consoled patients and assured them of adequate medical care. Shettima commended Governor Diri for visiting the accident scene and coordinating the state’s response, and acknowledged the efforts of the National Emergency Management Agency, the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency, the Nigerian Red Cross Society, the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, local divers and community volunteers. Governor Diri announced that the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills of all survivors and assured bereaved families that they would not be abandoned. On arrival in Yenagoa, the Vice President was received by Governor Diri, Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Senator Heineken Lokpobiri; Niger Delta Development Commission Managing Director, Dr Samuel Ogbuku; Bayelsa State APC Chairman, Dr Dennis Otiotio; and Niger Delta River Basin Development Authority Managing Director, Prince Ebitimi Amgbare. Members of the National Assembly, the Bayelsa State House of Assembly and the State Executive Council were also present.
